    For grown-ups: what this practices
    Each stop offers five levels — Preschool (ages 3–4), Kindergarten (age 5), 1st Grade (age 6), 2nd Grade (age 7), and 3rd Grade (age 8) — drawn from the Utah Core Standards for Early Learning and the Kindergarten, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Grade Cores. A round is 6 questions at whichever level is selected; every completed round earns at least one star, so nothing here is a "fail" — missed answers just get another gentle try.

    Why the stops are in this order. The National Reading Panel's "five pillars" of reading instruction build in a sequence: phonemic/phonological awareness (hearing and playing with sounds), then phonics (connecting those sounds to letters), then fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension (using both to read and understand real text). So Rhyme River (sound play) now comes before ABC Trailhead (letter-sound matching), which comes before the new Story Cove stop — where preschoolers match a spoken phrase to a picture, kindergartners read one decodable sentence and answer a question about it, and 1st graders read a short two-sentence passage and answer a comprehension question. That's the actual point of the earlier phonics work, so it gets its own stop instead of stopping at single letters and words.

    Look-alike letters. Reading researcher Tim Shanahan notes there's no single research-proven "best" order for teaching letters — but there is broad agreement on a few things: teach frequent letters before rare ones, mix consonants and vowels early, and keep visually or phonetically similar letters (like b and d, or p and q) apart at first. All 26 letters now appear in the letter games, but at Preschool look-alike letters are never shown next to each other as choices.

    Daily campfire. Finishing a trek (a round of 6 questions) adds a log to today's campfire; the daily goal (3 treks by default, adjustable in the dashboard) lights the fire, and playing on consecutive days builds a streak. Keyboard Camp builds first typing skills — and says each letter out loud as it is typed — finding letter keys at Preschool, typing short words at Kindergarten, and typing words and their own name in 1st Grade. Questions answered right on the first try are held back for a while so practice keeps moving on to fresh ones, while missed questions keep coming back until they are right.

    Campfire Circle & Compare Ridge. Two newer stops follow the school's family handouts: Campfire Circle covers feelings, family members and relatives, staying safe, and the weekly vocabulary words; Compare Ridge covers big/small and bigger/longer/heavier, position words (top, bottom, left, right, between), open and closed shapes, and the sides and corners of shapes. My Trail Sign now also asks the first letter, last letter and number of letters in the explorer's name, and Health Hollow adds a body map (head, shoulders, knees and feet) and texture words.

    2nd Grade. The fourth level follows the Utah 2nd Grade Core. Rhyme River covers silent e, vowel teams, syllables and blends; ABC Trailhead covers spelling, word endings, plurals, contractions and sentences; Story Cove has longer passages, main idea, fact versus opinion and word meanings; Critter Count works with numbers to 1,000, even and odd, and skip counting; Base Camp Math adds and subtracts to 100 and covers coins, clocks, arrays and word problems; Shape Overlook covers faces and sides and equal parts; Compare Ridge uses rulers and bar graphs; Nature Notebook covers matter, Earth and plants; Health Hollow covers body systems and safety; and Community Camp adds laws, maps, communities and more about Utah.

    3rd Grade. The fifth level follows the Utah 3rd Grade Core. Rhyme River covers prefixes, suffixes, homophones and syllables; ABC Trailhead covers parts of speech, verb tenses, possessives, commas and spelling; Story Cove covers theme, cause and effect, figurative language and text features; Critter Count covers rounding, fractions on a number line and equivalent fractions; Pattern Pass covers multiplying patterns and input-output tables; Base Camp Math covers multiplication and division facts, area, perimeter and elapsed time; Shape Overlook covers quadrilaterals, angles and symmetry; Nature Notebook covers forces, weather and life cycles; and Community Camp covers government, economics and maps.

    Community Camp & the newest skills. Community Camp (Stop 16) covers community helpers, rules and manners, needs and wants, simple maps, goods and services, jobs and money, and facts about Utah. These skills were added after comparing the app to the Utah early-learning and K-1 core standards: counting syllables, beginning / ending / middle sounds, blending letters into words, letter teams (sh, ch, th, wh) and compound words in Rhyme River; number order, teen numbers, counting by tens, place value, skip counting and comparing numbers in Critter Count; putting together and taking away in Base Camp Math; measuring length in Compare Ridge; main idea in Story Cove; light, sound, plants and seasons in Nature Notebook; and healthy habits in Health Hollow.

    Color Canyon. Utah's Core Standards for Early Learning list "recognize and name multiple colors" as a Fine Arts skill for 4-year-olds, so it earned its own stop. Preschool is pure color recognition (matching a color swatch, no words to lean on); Kindergarten connects a color name to a real object (an apple is red, a blueberry is blue); 1st Grade moves into basic color mixing — red and blue make purple, blue and yellow make green, red and yellow make orange.

    Health Hollow. Utah's Core Standards for Early Learning list naming major body parts under Health, Safety & Nutrition, so Preschool is pure point-to-it recognition — eyes, ears, arms, toes, and the rest. Kindergarten steps up to function ("what do you use to see?"), a distinct and harder skill than labeling alone. 1st Grade formalizes that into the five senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch) plus a first look at simple body systems — the heart, lungs, brain, and bones — matching how NGSS-aligned 1st grade life science introduces structure and function in the body.
